kypExtensions.summary: The pattern/trap/pivot/mini-case attack structure layered over the source's two subsections.
kypExtensions.rationale: First Aid supplies the two definitional subsections and the four-process blocker list; the attack structure is a KYP design.

kypExtensions.summary: The three-anchor reading of any pain stem (ANCHOR 1 — SORT THE PAIN: nociceptive = a TRANSMITTED signal 'in response to mechanical, thermal, or chemical stimuli' (the stimulus is the start of the story); neuropathic = 'neuronal dysfunction of the CNS or PNS' with 'upregulation and persistent activation of voltage-gated Na+ channels' (the nerve is the story — no stimulus needed). ANCHOR 2 — IF NOCICEPTIVE, FIND THE FIBER: Aδ = sharp, acute; C = dull, throbbing, chronic (first jab vs slow burn). ANCHOR 3 — LOCATE THE STEP, THEN READ THE BLOCKER LIST: Transduction → local anesthetics, α2-agonists, gabapentinoids, NSAIDs, acetaminophen, glucocorticoids; Transmission → local anesthetics, α2-agonists, opioids; Modulation → TCAs, SSRIs, SNRIs, gabapentinoids; Perception → α2-agonists, opioids, TCAs, SSRIs, SNRIs) — KYP's synthesis of the section's own list into one reading order (pain type → fiber → step → drug).
kypExtensions.rationale: The source prints the four process lines as a flat list without a reading protocol; the pain-type-first, then-fiber, then-step order is KYP's design (every drug name and process assignment is the book's own).
kypExtensions.location: core.keyIdea + mechanisms[0] + the visual's reading-rule strip

kypExtensions.summary: The anatomical station labels that SEAT the four processes — transduction at the nociceptor terminal (TRPV → Ca2+ influx → Na+ channel activation), transmission along Aδ/C fibers and up the ascending pathway, modulation at the dorsal-horn synapse and the descending control system, perception at the thalamus/cortex — are KYP extensions beyond the book's printed set: the page prints NO pathway diagram, NO dorsal-horn/spinothalamic/thalamus/cortex chain, NO substance P/glutamate, NO gate-control theory (verified against the text layer; pinned as this manifest's PAGE-STRUCTURE FINDING). The BLOCKER MATRIX (which class blocks which step: local anesthetics = transduction + transmission; α2-agonists = transduction + transmission + perception — three of four; opioids = transmission + perception; gabapentinoids = transduction + modulation; TCAs/SSRIs/SNRIs = modulation + perception; NSAIDs, acetaminophen, glucocorticoids = transduction only) is KYP's pivot of the book's own four printed lines — every cell is the book's own drug-class assignment; the matrix view itself is KYP.
kypExtensions.rationale: The book prints the four process lines separately; the step × class matrix (and the 'α2-agonists block three of the four' pattern it exposes) and the anatomical seating of each process are KYP's synthesis. Substance P, glutamate, and gate-control theory are deliberately NOT used — they are not printed on the page.
kypExtensions.location: blocks[2] the blocker matrix + mechanisms + the visual's station flow and matrix strip

kypExtensions.summary: The four KYP-original mnemonics (1 — TWO TICKETS, THEN TWO MORE: Transduction → Transmission → Modulation → Perception — the four T-M-T-P stations of every pain signal (stimulus becomes signal; signal travels; signal is tuned; signal is felt). 2 — DELTA IS THE DASH, C IS THE CRAWL: Aδ fibers = sharp, acute (first jab); C fibers = dull, throbbing, chronic (slow burn). 3 — α2 BLOCKS THREE OF FOUR: α2-agonists sit on transduction, transmission, AND perception — every station but modulation; OPIOIDS OWN THE ROAD AND THE ROOM (transmission + perception); NSAIDs ONLY THE STARTING LINE (transduction). 4 — NO STIMULUS, STILL PAIN: neuropathic pain is the upregulated, persistently active voltage-gated Na+ channel's fault — 'Example: diabetic peripheral neuropathy.' The Pain transmission section prints NO margin mnemonic — all four codes are KYP-original designs.
kypExtensions.rationale: Book 235's Pain transmission section prints NO mnemonic; all four codes are KYP-original designs built on the section's own printed lines.

notes: Census (pdfimages + text layer): NO raster images on the page (pdfimages -list returned zero rows for pdf 257) — the Pain transmission section is TYPESET TEXT ONLY in the LOWER portion of pdf 257 (book 235): the Nociceptive pain subsection (the definition sentence with its three stimulus modalities; the TRPV sentence — 'Transient receptor potential vanilloid ligand receptors cause Ca2+ influx–induced Na+ channel activation.'; the fiber sentence — Aδ = sharp, acute; C = dull, throbbing, chronic; and the four-process list with a blocker class set per process) and the Neuropathic pain subsection (CNS/PNS neuronal dysfunction; voltage-gated Na+ channel upregulation + persistent activation; diabetic peripheral neuropathy as the worked example), carried verbatim in the note's first table block. SECTION EXTENT: the section ENDS on pdf 257 — pdf 258 (book 236) opens the SEPARATE pending 'Micturition control' section (258-side boundary pinned). PAGE-STRUCTURE FINDING: the page prints NO pathway diagram and NO neurotransmitter account — the anticipated dorsal-horn → spinothalamic-tract → thalamus → cortex chain, substance P / glutamate, and the gate-control theory are NOT printed on this page; the book's own pathway frame is the FOUR-PROCESS LIST (Transduction/Transmission/Modulation/Perception), and the only anatomy printed is peripheral (nociceptor + TRPV; Aδ vs C fibers) plus the neuropathic Na+ channel. The ascending-station labels used to seat the four processes in the note and visual (dorsal-horn synapse, spinothalamic tract, thalamus/cortex, descending modulation) are KYP extensions beyond the book's printed set, flagged wherever they appear; substance P/glutamate and gate-control theory are NOT used. The blocker matrix (step × class) is KYP's pivot of the book's own four printed lines — every cell is the book's own assignment. The registry visual (PainTransmissionMap) is an ORIGINAL_KYP_ADAPTATION — an original KYP pain-process map synthesized from the section's own sentences (the stimulus band; the TRANSDUCTION node with the TRPV → Ca2+ → Na+ glyph; the Aδ/C fiber-split card; the MODULATION and PERCEPTION nodes; the NEUROPATHIC contrast panel; the blocker matrix; the four-code strip) — no source artwork exists to reproduce (no figure on the page). EXCLUSIONS: the 'Acetylcholine receptors' section in the UPPER portion of this SAME page is the COMPLETED topic PH12 'acetylcholine-receptors' (EXCLUDED; boundary pinned); pdf 256's lower portion is the COMPLETED topic PH11 'autonomic-receptors' (EXCLUDED; 256-side boundary pinned); pdf 258 opens the SEPARATE pending 'Micturition control' section (258-side boundary pinned). The clinical anchors that extend past the source page (clonidine/dexmedetomidine as the α2-agonists; lidocaine/bupivacaine as the local anesthetics; gabapentin/pregabalin as the gabapentinoids; amitriptyline/duloxetine as the TCA/SNRI; capsaicin as the TRPV agonist; the diabetic workup behind the neuropathy example) are flagged as KYP clinical anchors wherever they appear. The section prints NO margin mnemonic — all four mnemonic codes are KYP-original. No copyrighted photographs exist on the page; nothing reproduced.
